source.title: Explaining the Implicit Neural Canvas: Connecting Pixels to Neurons by Tracing Their Contributions
source.authors: Namitha Padmanabhan; M. Gwilliam; Pulkit Kumar; Shishira R. Maiya; Max Ehrlich; Abhinav Shrivastava

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own measurements of neuron-to-pixel representations in visual implicit neural representations (INRs), a different model setting from the claim. It does not test the listed claims about language models, explanation fidelity on held-out activations, or the stated interpretability shares.
record.gate_note: The study measures contribution maps and representation patterns in FFN and NeRV INRs. These results bear on neuron representations generally, but do not measure how many neurons have one or two named jobs, test explanations on unseen activations, or evaluate the versions' specific claims. Its figure-only plots are not recorded as numerical results.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes how neurons in small implicit neural representations (FFN and NeRV, overfit on single videos or frames) contribute to output pixels. It does not count neurons with one main job and tests no language models. It does not examine InceptionV1 or polysemantic neurons, compare tools or architectures for interpretable share, build attribution graphs, or score explanations on held-out activations. None of its results bear on any version. It neither tests nor uses the claim, so 'tests'/T3 is wrong; T6 fits.
record.authors_conclusion: Essentially correct. The authors conclude INRs lack high-level object semantics but are biased toward color and edges, and are largely space-agnostic. Representations are distributed, NeRV contribution changes over time are driven by motion, and neurons can be clustered by contribution maps into recurring types.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes XINC, measuring contributions from INR neurons to image pixels and analyzing their spatial and feature-group patterns. It does not use the language-model neuron-explanation audit or score explanations on held-out activations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported representation patterns differ between FFN and NeRV and across layers; the paper notes a NeRV Block 3 exception in its spatial-cluster comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: In small video/image INRs (FFN, NeRV), neuron contribution maps track low-level attributes (color, edges, textures) more than space or object class. Representations are distributed, and Gabor-feature clustering groups neurons into recurring 'types' across seeds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neurons in implicit neural representations encode low-level scene attributes in a distributed way rather than object-level semantics.

record.problems: The paper studies selected video examples and reports many results qualitatively or in figures; it does not test whether its descriptions predict activations on held-out inputs or quantify a share of interpretable neurons.

untested.parts: Shares across other language models, dense and MoE, at scale.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron, pose feature, recursive generalization vs superposition.
Causes of messy late-layer neurons; interpretable share rising with tools or architectures.
Neuron-level attribution graphs vs replacement models.
Whether explanations from activating examples predict firing on new inputs.
Simulation-based automated scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T3 relation conflicts with its own assessment that every version is not_tested. Reclassified to discusses/T6. The paper is a vision-INR interpretability method (XINC) with no connection to the claim's neuron-share or explanation-scoring versions.

versions.untested_parts: The Qwen3-32B audit shares and neuron-pole job counts.
Language-model comparisons, dense and mixture-of-experts models, and scaling to the stated parameter range.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose detection, and recursive generalization versus superposition.
The stated causes of messy late-layer neurons, comparisons of tools or architectures for interpretability, and the estimated interpretable-neuron shares.
Attribution graphs, their ability to explain behavior, and comparison with replacement models or reconstruction error.
Whether explanations fit activating examples but fail to predict activations on new inputs.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulated activations on new text.

rows.subject: FFN
rows.operation_detail: Measured neuron contribution maps to represented image pixels and described patterns across layers.

conditions.value: Selected video frames; videos from Cityscapes-VPS and VIPSeg

rows.measure: Qualitative patterns in neuron contribution maps.
rows.value: The paper describes early-layer Fourier patterns and later-layer maps representing more of the image, with Fourier artifacts; it says neuron behavior is not simply to represent some pixels, but learns low-level scene attributes.
rows.note: This is a reported characterization of INR neurons, not a count of neurons with a single named job or a test of explanation accuracy.

rows.subject: NeRV
rows.operation_detail: Measured neuron contribution maps to represented image pixels and described patterns across layers.

conditions.value: Selected videos from Cityscapes-VPS and VIPSeg

rows.measure: Qualitative patterns in neuron contribution maps.
rows.value: The paper describes neurons capturing varied features including edges, textures, colors, and depth; head-layer maps are reminiscent of image-processing filters.
rows.note: The authors characterize these as low-level scene attributes and report a lack of high-level object semantics.

rows.subject: FFN
rows.operation_detail: Compared neuron contribution variation across instance, RGB, Gabor-feature, and spatial gridcell pixel clusters.
rows.measure: Variance of normalized contribution differences across clusters.
rows.baseline: Gridcell clusters as the spatial reference; expected contribution computed from cluster area.
rows.value: The text reports relatively little meaningful correlation with space and higher variance for instance, RGB, and Gabor clusters; it says the top 25% of instance, RGB, and Gabor variances are almost all higher than even the highest gridcell variance.
rows.note: Numeric variance values are shown only in the figure and are not transcribed. The text interprets the pattern as low-level rather than class-level semantics.

rows.subject: NeRV
rows.operation_detail: Compared neuron contribution variation across instance, RGB, Gabor-feature, and spatial gridcell pixel clusters.
rows.measure: Variance of normalized contribution differences across clusters.
rows.baseline: Gridcell clusters as the spatial reference; expected contribution computed from cluster area.
rows.value: The text reports relatively little meaningful correlation with space and higher variance for instance, RGB, and Gabor clusters; it notes an exception in NeRV Block 3, which seems to have some meaningful gridcell correlation.
rows.note: Numeric variance values are shown only in the figure. The authors say the overall pattern still holds because the top 25% of instance, RGB, and Gabor variances are almost all above the highest gridcell variance.
rows.check: State 'partial' is relative to no version. The row measures INR contribution variance across pixel clusters, which bears on no version.

rows.subject: FFN
rows.operation_detail: Counted pixels to which each neuron contributes meaningfully, using a contribution-ratio threshold.

conditions.value: Reciprocal of the number of neurons in the layer

rows.measure: Number of image pixels represented meaningfully per neuron.
rows.value: Nearly 50% of the neurons in FFN Layer 2 have almost no contributions.
rows.note: The paper relates this observation to dead neurons and compression, not to a count of interpretable jobs.
rows.check: The ~50% near-zero-contribution neurons in FFN Layer 2 are dead neurons in a 33k-parameter INR. This is not a share of interpretable or single-job neurons, and state 'partial' has no referent.

rows.subject: NeRV
rows.operation_detail: Measured the density of neurons contributing significantly at each image location, at two contribution thresholds.

conditions.value: 10th and 50th percentile of sorted raw contributions

rows.measure: Percentage of neurons contributing significant portions of pixels.
rows.value: The text says higher thresholds highlight areas with the highest neuron density and reveal an overwhelming bias for edges with NeRV.
rows.note: This measures spatial contribution density, not the fraction of neurons with a single interpretable job.

rows.subject: FFN
rows.operation_detail: Compared summed neuron contribution maps with image intensity.
rows.measure: Relationship between aggregate contribution magnitude and image intensity.
rows.baseline: Raw image intensity, defined by summing color channels.
rows.value: The text says Layer 3 contributions are largely consistent with intensity, while Layer 2 also over-represents people relative to intensity; the authors report that edges and textures are also attended to beyond intensity.
rows.note: The comparison is qualitative in the text; plotted magnitudes are not transcribed.
rows.check: Contribution vs intensity comparison bears on no version; state 'partial' has no referent.

rows.subject: NeRV
rows.operation_detail: Compared summed neuron contribution maps with image intensity.
rows.measure: Relationship between aggregate contribution magnitude and image intensity.
rows.baseline: Raw image intensity, defined by summing color channels.
rows.value: The text reports a correspondence between high contribution and high intensity, alongside attention to edges and textures beyond intensity; it also describes an edge bias and unequal contributions to different edges.
rows.note: The comparison is qualitative in the text; plotted magnitudes are not transcribed.
rows.check: Contribution vs intensity comparison bears on no version; state 'partial' has no referent.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
